uncited: What sets this family apart from its siblings is its specific focus on line-based abstraction rather than surface shading or contour outlines; it distinguishes itself from [Face-based volume rendering with edge highlights](2453-face-based-volume-rendering-with-edge-highlights.md) by generating lines that represent intrinsic surface properties (like curvature) rather than just silhouette edges, and from [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by often utilizing vector-oriented or texture-based approaches that are viewpoint-independent or analytically derived, rather than purely image-space depth-difference extraction.
They rely on explicit analytical representations of the model or volume data.
The distinction between analytical and pixel-based methods is well-established in the literature.
Hertzmann provided a useful survey of image space outline generation algorithms [Her99].
Specific applications to volume data emerged in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Interrante et al. introduced the principal direction line texture technique starting with [Int97], leveraging perceptual psychology literature [GIHL00] to justify the use of principal curvature directions.
In 2001, Csébfalvi et al. presented a fast NPR volume visualization technique based on object contours, which relied on locally high gradient values to estimate physical boundaries [CMH+01].
